\title{What Does an Auxiliary Prototypicality Target Actually Buy?\\
A Control-Task Analysis of Cross-Corpus Speech Emotion Recognition}

\begin{abstract}
TODO. Must state, in order: (i) auxiliary heads are widely reported to improve
SER but are almost never validated against a capacity-matched control;
(ii) we add an auxiliary head predicting the within-class, covariance-whitened
VAD residual; (iii) against a control task whose target is permuted within the
batch, the effect on IEMOCAP is +1.62 neutral-vs-rest AUC and +0.72 UAR, five
of five seeds; (iv) on SAMSEMO the permuted control alone recovers most of the
apparent gain, which we report rather than suppress; (v) an ablation ladder
shows the covariance whitening, not the auxiliary head itself, is what moves
the neutral boundary.
\end{abstract}

\begin{keywords}
speech emotion recognition, cross-corpus generalisation, auxiliary tasks,
control tasks, annotator agreement
\end{keywords}

\subsection{Auxiliary prototypicality target}
\label{sec:target}
% For a sample with label c and normalised VAD vector v, the target is
%   r = W_c (v - mu_c)
% where mu_c is the class centroid fitted on the training split and W_c is the
% whitening matrix from that class's covariance. The head is a single linear
% layer on the fused representation, trained with MSE at weight 1.0.
TODO

\subsection{Control task}
\label{sec:control}
% The target is permuted within the batch. Same head, same parameter count,
% same gradient path, same target marginal distribution; only the
% sample-to-target pairing is destroyed. Any gain of the real arm over this
% control is attributable to the target's information content rather than to
% added capacity.

\section{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}
% Train: MSP-Podcast. Zero-shot eval: IEMOCAP, SAMSEMO. Four classes
% (neutral, happy, sad, angry). Five seeds throughout; all comparisons are
% paired per seed, since arms correlate strongly across seeds and the paired
% difference has roughly half the standard deviation of the raw metric.
% Metrics: UAR, and neutral-vs-rest ROC-AUC computed on 1 - P(neutral),
% which is threshold free and therefore does not depend on where argmax
